description: Screenshot of a tweet from Donald J. Trump (@realDonaldTrump), verified account, dated May 3 2020. The tweet (a continuation, opening with ellipsis) claims the 'Fake News' got it wrong and that his early travel ban on China saved tens of thousands of lives, and that admitted travelers were heavily scrutinized and tested U.S. citizens.
text: Donald J. Trump. @realDonaldTrump. ....Fake News got it wrong again, as always, and tens of thousands of lives were saved by my EARLY BAN of China into our Country. The people that we're allowed were heavily scrutinized and tested U.S. citizens, and as such, I welcome them with open arms!. 1:18 PM - May 3, 2020 - Twitter for iPhone
flags: Tweet's claims about lives saved by the travel ban are the author's assertion, not verified

description: Black-and-white meme built on a tightly cropped, high-contrast half-face portrait of Donald Trump staring into the camera. White block-letter captions above and below read 'STAY WITH ME DEPLORABLES' and 'YOU'LL LOVE HOW THIS MOVIE ENDS', invoking the 'deplorables' label and the Q-community 'enjoy the show'/movie framing.
text: STAY WITH ME DEPLORABLES. YOU'LL LOVE HOW THIS MOVIE ENDS

description: Black-and-white graphic pairing a portrait of Barack Obama, eyes glancing down and to the side, with a dictionary-style definition of 'renegade'. Side text notes that Renegade was Obama's Secret Service codename and asserts it was 'personally selected'; the definition emphasizes betrayal, with synonyms like traitor and defector. A small 'Q' mark sits in the lower right corner.
text: ren-e-gade. /ˈrenə.gād/. Noun. 1. a person who deserts and betrays an organization, country, or set of Principles. Synonyms:. Traitor, defector. Deserter, turncoat, rebel. mutineer. Obama's personally selected Secret Service Codename:. Renegade. Q
flags: The claim that Obama personally selected the codename is the meme's assertion; Secret Service codenames are conventionally assigned from a candidate list
Definition wording is slanted toward 'traitor' rather than a neutral dictionary entry

description: Screenshot of page 2 of a U.S. Attorney General memorandum titled 'Balancing Public Safety with the Preservation of Civil Rights'. The excerpt states that policies unthinkable in regular times have become commonplace, that the Constitution is not suspended in times of crisis, and closes with thanks for service. Consistent with Attorney General William Barr's April 27 2020 memo to prosecutors on COVID-19 restrictions, though no author or date is visible on this page.
text: Memorandum from the Attorney General. Page 2. Subject: Balancing Public Safety with the Preservation of Civil Rights. Many policies that would be unthinkable in regular times have become commonplace in recent weeks, and we do not want to unduly interfere with the important efforts of state and local officials to protect the public. But the Constitution is not suspended in times of crisis. We must therefore be vigilant to ensure its protections are preserved, at the same time that the public is protected.. I thank you for your attention to this important initiative and for your service to our country.
flags: Attribution to William Barr and the April 2020 date are inferred from content and context, not visible on the page

description: Quote graphic on a black background pairing Rembrandt Peale's portrait of Thomas Jefferson with a quotation about tyranny and liberty attributed to Jefferson: when the people fear the government there is tyranny, when the government fears the people there is liberty.
text: When the people fear the government there is tyranny,. when the government fears the people there is liberty.. ~ Thomas Jefferson
flags: Attribution is the meme's claim: this quotation is widely regarded as spurious — Monticello lists no evidence Jefferson said or wrote it
